dev_notes: One file per agent in src/agents/ (claude.mjs, codex.mjs, gemini.mjs, custom.mjs), each with the headless command line, a parser for its event stream and its resume command; index.mjs is the registry and resolves --run (a bare --run reads $LEDGER_AGENT or config.json "agent"), runner.mjs spawns it in the project root with the prompt on stdin. src/prompt.mjs holds TASKS: how to call each brief and the stamp to check afterwards; an agent that exits without it returns exit code 3. Claude runs with acceptEdits and an allowlist of ledger and read-only git commands; Codex with --sandbox workspace-write. The Claude and Codex adapters were tested against the real CLIs; the Gemini one follows its documented headless mode and has not been run against a live install.

history.name: Handing a task to a coding agent
history.description: The commands that prepare work for a coding agent — bootstrap, audit, review, redraft check and style rewrite — print a prompt for you to paste. Add --copy to put it on the clipboard, or --run claude, codex or gemini to hand it to that agent and wait; any other command that reads a prompt on stdin works too. When the agent stops, you see its last message, whether it recorded what its task asks for, and the command that resumes its session. Nothing is handed to an agent unless you pass --run.

The commands that prepare work for a coding agent, bootstrap, audit, compose, verify, paths brief, redraft check and style rewrite, print a prompt for you to paste. Add --copy to put it on the clipboard, or --run claude, codex or gemini to hand it to that agent and wait. When the agent stops, you see its last message, whether it left what its task asks for, and the command that resumes its session. Nothing is handed to an agent unless you pass --run.

events.what: The agent tasks were bootstrap, audit, review, redraft check and style rewrite. ledger summary joins them, with the same ways to deliver its prompt, so the lists an edition opens with can be handed to an agent like the audit and the review. See “Summary of changes”.
compose, verify and paths brief are agent tasks; summary and review are not.
events.why: Compose and verify replace the summary and the review, and saying which code each entry lives in needs something that can read the code.
